description:
lib.rs:281-301 inserts Severity::Notice between Info and Warn, mid-enum. The Severity test severity_ordering_is_info_notice_warn_error_fatal at lib.rs:1934-1942 pins the ordering explicitly: assert!(Severity::Info < Severity::Notice); …

Defense: inserting a variant in the middle of a #[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)] enum silently reorders existing variants. Without an explicit ordering test, a future contributor adding 'Critical' (or any other variant) in the wrong position would silently break every consumer that filters by '>= Warn'. The explicit test catches this at compile-error-via-test-fail time.

The PartialOrd derivation depends on declaration order. The test makes that order load-bearing rather than an accident.

What a contributor might suggest changing: 'just sort the Severity enum alphabetically' — would break the ordering. Or 'use a custom PartialOrd impl with explicit cases' — more code, equivalent behavior, easier to break with a refactor. The current shape (declaration order + ordering test) is the simplest correct option.

Lock this in. Add similar ordering pins to any other deriving-PartialOrd enum in the workspace.
title: Severity::Notice slotted into existing ordering with explicit pin test
